stresses: SCHEMA FINDING, escalated prominently (see RECONCILIATION.md and the leaf-level note below): this transcript narrates TWO real, current, fully-independent HVAC systems -- a furnace (manufacturer/model/fuel-question/year) and a separately-standalone-duct central AC (its own attic ducts, insulation, leakage) -- explicitly NOT sharing ducts, with identity detail belonging to one and duct detail belonging to the other. The single-hvac-instance schema (schema.ts's own documented 'Cardinality' divergence) cannot represent this house; ONE instance is chosen (the furnace, as the more fully-detailed, explicitly-reaffirmed system) and the loss is real, not resolved by annotation. Also: THE named silent-drop trap -- equipment is unambiguous (furnace) but the auditor explicitly declines the fuel ('I can't tell you the fuel on this one') and this must land as declared_absent, not silently collapse to the same 'unmentioned' a truly-never-discussed fuel would get. Two more individually-declared absences stack alongside it (model year unreadable; attic depth explicitly not measured, only the R-value eyeballed) -- mirroring the worked example's R-value/depth split. A genuine partial value ('model G-something') that is incomplete but still a real, stated fragment, not a pure non-answer. A clean, low-ambiguity wall-insulation call ('some, but poor' -> 'Poorly') matching schema.ts's own doc-comment example almost verbatim.

hvac.hvacSystemEquipmentType.sourceSpan: heating is a furnace, forced air, I can see the supply plenum coming off it.

arguable.note: SCHEMA FINDING, not a within-statement ambiguity: this transcript describes TWO full, independently-unambiguous standalone-duct systems on one property -- a furnace ('heating is a furnace, forced air ... supply plenum') and a central AC ('The AC's got its own ducts up in the attic, standalone, separate from anything the furnace does. Central AC, standalone ducts.') -- each one individually clear about NOT sharing ducts with the other (so this is NOT rule 6's conflated-axis pattern; the shared/standalone axis is explicitly resolved for both, hence no `symmetric`). The ambiguity is schema.ts's own documented 'Cardinality' divergence: this schema models exactly ONE hvac instance, so a second, equally-well-described system 'lands on the same leaves as the first and the reviewer sees the collision' (schema.ts file header). The furnace is chosen because it is mentioned first and re-affirmed with an explicit correction ('Let me be clear: heating is a furnace...'), and because it carries the manufacturer/model/fuel/year detail cluster -- but this is a judgment call about WHICH system occupies the one slot, not a resolution of what either system actually is. hvac.hvacDuctLocation/hvacDuctLeakage/hvacDuctInsulation below describe the AC's attic ductwork, not the furnace's -- so this record's hvac.* leaves, taken TOGETHER, describe two different physical systems. THE LOSS IS REAL: no encoding of this record recovers 'both systems, correctly attributed' from a single hvac instance; a downstream consumer reading this record alone would believe the furnace has bare, disconnected, very-leaky attic ducts, when those ducts belong to the AC. Recorded here, not solved.

It is explicitly incomplete ('I couldn't get the full model number off the corner it was jammed into'), so a model that leaves this null instead of inventing digits is a defensible caution, not a penalized miss.

notes._general: No blanket negation ('no tests', 'no water heater', etc.) appears anywhere in this transcript, so there are no `disclaimers` entries -- the window, dhw, health, and basedata groups, plus attic.atticHasKneeWall/atticRoofType and wall.wallExteriorWallSiding, are never brought up at all and correctly resolve to the default 'unmentioned'. The 'no wait' self-correction in paragraph 2 ('up in the attic there's an air handler, no wait, the furnace itself is in the closet...') is a location clarification, not a value retraction of any leaf here -- no equipment-type member was actually stated before the correction, so it is not recorded as `retracted`. wall.wallCavityInsulation (the R-value number) is left unmentioned on purpose: 'a couple inches of old batt' states a thickness, not an R-value, and the wall group's only numeric leaf is R-value -- there is no depth/thickness write target for walls the way attic has both, so this has no home rather than being forced into the R-value leaf (rule 9). The furnace's own physical location ('the furnace itself is in the closet') has no write target either -- there is no equipment-location leaf, only hvacDuctLocation, which this file uses for the AC's duct location instead.
